text.arabic_uthmani: وَيَدْعُ ٱلْإِنسَٰنُ بِٱلشَّرِّ دُعَآءَهُۥ بِٱلْخَيْرِ ۖ وَكَانَ ٱلْإِنسَٰنُ عَجُولًۭا

words.gloss_range: coordinating and resumptive connector opening the diagnostic statement

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: the opening verb of human calling

words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) opens 17:11 as a bridge from the warning in 17:10 into a fresh human diagnosis, carrying the prior punishment statement rather than leaving it behind. It launches directly into {{ar:يَدْعُ}} ({{tr:yadʿu}}), so the ayah is continuation with a turn rather than a detached proverb. The later {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) creates a paired two-beat frame: human invocation first, explanatory haste second.

topics.headline: bridge from warning to diagnosis
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the human diagnosis remains tied to the preceding warning in 17:10 while opening a new general statement.
topics.reason: QAC identifies coordination with the preceding context, and the rows coherently preserve both coordination and resumption.

topics.headline: connector fused to action
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears and sees the transition enter directly into the verb of calling.
topics.reason: The written sequence supports an attached launch into {{ar:يَدْعُ}} ({{tr:yadʿu}}).

topics.headline: paired clause openings
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the paired {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) openings that organize the ayah as observation followed by diagnosis.
topics.reason: The two clauses are particle-opened and attachment evidence separates the first verbal clause from the later {{ar:كَانَ}} ({{tr:kāna}}) clause.

words.gloss_range: active imperfect invocation, locally directed through a bāʾ content frame toward harm
words.root_gloss_range: calling, summoning, petitioning, naming, and claim-making branches; the local Form I frame selects petition or invocation while broader branches remain background

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: cognate verbal noun measuring the act

words.prose: {{ar:يَدْعُ}} ({{tr:yadʿu}}) makes the human visibly responsible for a recurring act of invocation. Its local frame is not a simple direct object: {{ar:بِٱلشَّرِّ}} ({{tr:bi-sh-sharri}}) supplies content through {{ar:بِـ}} ({{tr:bi-}}), so the human petitions for harm and, by petitioning, draws the harmful object toward himself. {{ar:دُعَآءَهُۥ}} ({{tr:duʿāʾahu}}) repeats the same root as the measuring noun, making the call name itself inside the clause. Broader {{ar:د ع و}} ({{tr:d-ʿ-w}}) branches are narrowed to petitionary calling here rather than naming, broadcasting, or legal claim, while 17:52 and 17:71 keep calling language alive later in the surah.

topics.headline: recurring active human invocation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the human is the active, recurring caller whose behavior needs explanation.
topics.reason: QAC marks {{ar:يَدْعُ}} ({{tr:yadʿu}}) as a 3ms imperfect active verb with {{ar:ٱلْإِنسَٰنُ}} ({{tr:al-insānu}}) as subject.

topics.headline: invocation through bāʾ content
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that harm is invoked through a prepositional content frame, not as a bare direct object.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence gives {{ar:بِٱلشَّرِّ}} ({{tr:bi-sh-sharri}}) as governed complement of the calling verb.

topics.headline: petition sense selected from broad root
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the richness of the calling root while keeping the local act as invocation rather than naming or claim-making.
topics.reason: The local Form I verb plus bāʾ complements and cognate maṣdar select prayer or petition; other branches remain background.

topics.headline: clipped written launch
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the visually clipped spelling at the action launch, with recitation preserving the long vowel.
topics.reason: QAC notes graphic dropping of the final wāw in {{ar:يَدْعُ}} ({{tr:yadʿu}}).

topics.headline: verb echoed by verbal noun
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the act of calling names itself inside the clause through {{ar:دُعَآءَهُۥ}} ({{tr:duʿāʾahu}}).
topics.reason: Attachment evidence identifies the later verbal noun as cognate accusative, so the root reprise is structural.

topics.headline: calling thread beyond the verse
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the human call in 17:11 anticipates later summons and related invocation scenes, including 17:52, 17:71, 41:49, and 10:11-12.
topics.reason: The rows give concrete references; they are retained as echoes without overriding local grammar.

words.gloss_range: definite singular generic human as explicit subject of the first invocation clause
words.root_gloss_range: human, familiarity, perception, and debated forgetting associations; local grammar selects the generic human subject while etymological pressure remains secondary
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلْإِنسَٰنُ}} ({{tr:al-insānu}}) makes the caller explicit and generic. The ayah is not about one named offender but about the human type, compressed into a singular definite subject. The debated pressure around perception, familiarity, and forgetting colors the misjudging human without replacing the local subject sense. When the same noun returns at word 9, the caller becomes the diagnosed bearer of haste, linking 17:11 to later human portraits in 17:67, 17:83, and 17:100.

topics.headline: generic human as explicit actor
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the act is assigned to the human type as such, not to an unnamed or isolated individual.
topics.reason: QAC and attachment data make the noun nominative subject of {{ar:يَدْعُ}} ({{tr:yadʿu}}), and the article supports generic reference.

topics.headline: perceiving yet forgetting human
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a lexical irony: the sensing or familiar human is also portrayed as one who forgets or fails to discern harm from good.
topics.reason: The derivational dispute is meaningful as pressure, but local grammar still selects the ordinary generic human noun.

topics.headline: first half of human refrain
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the first human label is designed to be heard again in the final diagnosis clause.
topics.reason: The repeated surface at words 3 and 9 is local and structurally ties action to diagnosis.

topics.headline: start of surah human portrait series
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that 17:11 begins a same-surah chain of human diagnostics that returns at 17:67, 17:83, and 17:100.
topics.reason: The inter-ayah rows give concrete same-surah references and preserve a real formulaic payoff.

topics.headline: species claim toward individual record
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the generic human diagnosis in 17:11 can lead into the individualized accountability language of 17:13.
topics.reason: The boundary row supplies a concrete forward reference and remains a discourse bridge.

words.gloss_range: definite harm or evil as the first invoked content pole in a bāʾ phrase
words.root_gloss_range: evil, harm, corruption, damage, and destructive negative valence; spark imagery may color the field but the local sense is harm or evil as a category

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: the definite harm noun inside the phrase

words.prose: {{ar:بِٱلشَّرِّ}} ({{tr:bi-sh-sharri}}) gives the first content of the human call: harm or evil is named before the comparison to good is revealed. The preposition primarily marks governed invoked content under {{ar:يَدْعُ}} ({{tr:yadʿu}}); causal or instrumental shades remain as the felt possibility that perceived harm provokes the call or becomes its medium. As a definite abstract noun, {{ar:ٱلشَّرِّ}} ({{tr:ash-sharri}}) is the recognized negative pole, carrying moral evil, physical harm, corruption, and even a scattering-damage image as pressure. Its matched opposite {{ar:بِٱلْخَيْرِ}} ({{tr:bi-l-khayri}}) forms the central mirror of the ayah: to the hasty human, the two poles can become practically interchangeable. The contrast also recalls 2:216 and later consequence language at 17:83.

topics.headline: harm as first invoked content
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that harm is the immediate content of the call before the verse reveals the comparison to good.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence binds the phrase to {{ar:يَدْعُ}} ({{tr:yadʿu}}) as a prepositional complement giving invoked content.

topics.headline: secondary bāʾ force pressure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the bāʾ can let harm feel like provocation or medium, while local syntax keeps it as called-for content.
topics.reason: The causal and instrumental possibilities survive as pressure, but QAC and attachment identify content complement as primary.

topics.headline: destructive negative field
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the requested pole includes harm, corruption, and destructive disorder, not just an abstract label of badness.
topics.reason: The lexical range supports a broad negative field, with spark imagery kept as root-image pressure.

topics.headline: central harm-good mirror
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that harm and good are made formally parallel even though they are moral opposites.
topics.reason: The two bāʾ phrases have matching syntax and definiteness, so the antithesis is structural as well as semantic.

topics.headline: known abstract harm pole
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the verse contrasts harm as a recognized category, not a merely comparative or indefinite bad thing.
topics.reason: The local form is a definite abstract noun in a prepositional phrase.

topics.headline: epistemic limit and consequence echoes
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the local harm-good confusion is illuminated by the knowing and not-knowing contrast of 2:216 and by harm touching the human at 17:83.
topics.reason: The rows provide concrete references, so the echoes are kept as parallels and consequences.

topics.headline: assimilated heavy sound against good pole
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the doubled, assimilated sound of the harm phrase contrast with the later good phrase inside the same frame.
topics.reason: The surface forms support the sound contrast between {{ar:بِٱلشَّرِّ}} ({{tr:bi-sh-sharri}}) and {{ar:بِٱلْخَيْرِ}} ({{tr:bi-l-khayri}}).

words.gloss_range: possessed verbal noun of invocation functioning as cognate accusative and comparison hinge
words.root_gloss_range: calling, appeal, invocation, prayer, and request; the local maṣdar makes the act of calling measurable between harm and good

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: finite verb echoed by the verbal noun

words.prose: {{ar:دُعَآءَهُۥ}} ({{tr:duʿāʾahu}}) turns {{ar:يَدْعُ}} ({{tr:yadʿu}}) into a measurable act: the human calls for harm with a calling like his own calling for good. The suffix makes the comparison personal, not a detached theory of prayer. The maṣdar makes the request-act itself concrete, including the pressure of appeal or distress-call, so the danger is not only wrong content but a full act of asking aimed the wrong way. Standing between {{ar:بِٱلشَّرِّ}} ({{tr:bi-sh-sharri}}) and {{ar:بِٱلْخَيْرِ}} ({{tr:bi-l-khayri}}), the word equates opposite invocations in manner and intensity, while its long vowels and hamza make the hinge audible.

topics.headline: calling measured by its own noun
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the verse compares the manner and intensity of calling, not merely two requested contents.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence marks the verbal noun as cognate accusative of {{ar:يَدْعُ}} ({{tr:yadʿu}}).

topics.headline: his own prayer as measure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the harmful call is measured against the human's own mode of asking for good.
topics.reason: The suffix in {{ar:دُعَآءَهُۥ}} ({{tr:duʿāʾahu}}) refers back to the generic human.

topics.headline: request-act made concrete
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the act of invocation itself becoming visible as a stable verbal noun.
topics.reason: The maṣdar form and lexical range support call, appeal, invocation, prayer, and request.

topics.headline: midpoint between harm and good
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the word sitting between the two bāʾ phrases and making opposite contents formally comparable.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence connects {{ar:بِٱلْخَيْرِ}} ({{tr:bi-l-khayri}}) to the verbal noun, completing the comparison.

topics.headline: formula and punishment mechanism
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the invocation formula links the prior punishment warning to the human mechanism that can call harm as if it were good, with a parallel at 41:49.
topics.reason: The concrete 41:49 and boundary evidence survive as discourse context.

topics.headline: echo and audible hinge
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the finite verb and verbal noun echo each other, with the hamza and long vowels slowing the comparison point.
topics.reason: The surface forms support both root echo and phonetic prominence at the comparison hinge.

words.gloss_range: definite good, benefit, or welfare as the comparison pole in the second bāʾ phrase
words.root_gloss_range: good, benefit, welfare, prosperity, and choosing or preference; local usage is definite abstract good rather than a comparative better-form

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: repeated preposition in both comparison poles

words.prose: {{ar:بِٱلْخَيْرِ}} ({{tr:bi-l-khayri}}) closes the first clause by naming the good pole against which the harmful call is measured. Its second {{ar:بِـ}} ({{tr:bi-}}) mirrors the first, making harm and good grammatically commensurable even while meaning keeps them opposed. The root range includes benefit, welfare, prosperity, and choosing, so the good here is the beneficial outcome that hasty invocation fails to discern. In context, 10:11 and 17:35 keep the good pole tied to divine non-hastening and measured judgment.

topics.headline: good completes comparison
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the first clause is not complete until the good pole closes the comparison.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence makes the phrase the complement inside the comparison around {{ar:دُعَآءَهُۥ}} ({{tr:duʿāʾahu}}).

topics.headline: good as benefit and discerned choice
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that good includes concrete benefit and the discernment of choice, precisely what haste corrupts.
topics.reason: The lexical range supports benefit, welfare, prosperity, and choosing or preferring as pressure around the local good pole.

topics.headline: formal mirror of harm phrase
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the good phrase is shaped to match the harm phrase, so the ear registers equivalence before meaning separates the poles.
topics.reason: Both phrases are definite abstract nouns governed by {{ar:بِـ}} ({{tr:bi-}}).

topics.headline: category not comparative ranking
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the phrase names good as a category, not counted goods or a relative better item.
topics.reason: The root has comparative and plural uses elsewhere, but the local form is singular definite abstract {{ar:ٱلْخَيْرِ}} ({{tr:al-khayri}}).

topics.headline: good in haste and measure fields
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the good pole belongs to a wider field where divine non-hastening in 10:11 and right measure in 17:35 expose human misjudgment.
topics.reason: The rows give concrete references and support a discourse payoff without adding a new local sense.

words.gloss_range: resumptive connector opening the explanatory kāna clause, with circumstantial pressure possible

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: state verb opening the diagnostic clause

words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) marks the turn from the completed harm-good comparison into the explanatory diagnosis. It prevents {{ar:كَانَ}} ({{tr:kāna}}) from being absorbed into the prior phrase and opens a new clause with its own subject and predicate. Circumstantial pressure remains possible, so the human calls while in a state of haste, but the local architecture is especially a resumptive pivot from observation to diagnosis. Its repeated short opening also pairs this clause with the first {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}), giving the ayah audible clause symmetry.

topics.headline: pivot into diagnosis
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the exact hinge where comparison ends and explanation begins.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence separates the first verbal clause from the coordinated {{ar:كَانَ}} ({{tr:kāna}}) clause.

topics.headline: while-being-hasty pressure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that haste can be heard as the condition accompanying the misdirected call, while the clause still functions as a fresh diagnosis.
topics.reason: The circumstantial reading is coherent, but QAC and clause evidence primarily support a resumptive explanatory clause.

topics.headline: second paired opening
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the second clause open in parallel with the first, reinforcing observation then diagnosis.
topics.reason: The repeated particle at both clause openings is local and audible.

words.gloss_range: perfect-form copular state verb assigning haste as an enduring predicate
words.root_gloss_range: being, existing, becoming, occurring, and formation branches; local Form I copula selects established state, not causative formation
words.prose: {{ar:كَانَ}} ({{tr:kāna}}) converts the first clause from observed action into state diagnosis: the human calls this way because the human is characterized by haste. The perfect form gives the predicate settledness rather than a merely past episode. The broader {{ar:ك و ن}} ({{tr:k-w-n}}) field is narrowed locally to Form I copular state, not causative formation. Within Sūrah 17, {{ar:كَانَ ٱلْإِنسَٰنُ}} ({{tr:kāna al-insānu}}) becomes part of a diagnostic series at 17:67 and 17:100, and the register shifts from the prior divine verdict into detached anthropological analysis, with the haste field developing at 17:18.

topics.headline: action explained as state
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the second clause explains the first action by naming an enduring human state.
topics.reason: QAC and attachment evidence make {{ar:كَانَ}} ({{tr:kāna}}) govern {{ar:ٱلْإِنسَٰنُ}} ({{tr:al-insānu}}) and {{ar:عَجُولًۭا}} ({{tr:ʿajūlan}}).

topics.headline: being field as local state
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that haste is placed in the field of being while local grammar blocks causative or formation readings.
topics.reason: The root family pressure is valid, but the local Form I defective copula selects established state.

topics.headline: settled perfect after recurring imperfect
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the aspectual contrast: recurring calling is followed by a settled diagnostic predicate.
topics.reason: The imperfect {{ar:يَدْعُ}} ({{tr:yadʿu}}) and perfect-form {{ar:كَانَ}} ({{tr:kāna}}) stand in adjacent clause sequence.

topics.headline: same-surah human diagnosis formula
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that this clause starts a same-surah formula of human portraits, with 17:67 and 17:100 as later examples.
topics.reason: The concrete references preserve the formulaic payoff; 17:18 is retained as a nearby development of the haste field.

topics.headline: common verb made specific by rare predicate
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the common state verb gains its local force from being paired with the rare final haste predicate.
topics.reason: Distributional commonness matters here because it points to the local specificity of the predicate pairing.

words.gloss_range: repeated definite generic human as ism kāna and bearer of the haste predicate
words.root_gloss_range: human, familiarity, perception, and debated forgetting associations; local grammar selects the repeated generic human as state-bearer

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: state verb governing the repeated human noun
haste predicate borne by the repeated human noun

words.prose: The second {{ar:ٱلْإِنسَٰنُ}} ({{tr:al-insānu}}) restates the same generic human where a pronoun could have sufficed. That repetition makes the caller of the first clause become the subject of {{ar:كَانَ}} ({{tr:kāna}}) and the bearer of {{ar:عَجُولًۭا}} ({{tr:ʿajūlan}}). Lexical pressure around perception or forgetting remains as color, but the main local payoff is structural: the human noun brackets the ayah, absorbs the prior group into a general human diagnosis, and makes the final haste predicate land as the answer to the whole human loop. The 21:37 parallel intensifies the relation, while 17:67 and 17:100 continue the same-surah diagnostic chain.

topics.headline: same generic human as state-bearer
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the same generic human who calls is explicitly renamed as the one diagnosed.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence makes the noun the ism of {{ar:كَانَ}} ({{tr:kāna}}), and repetition ties it to word 3.

topics.headline: perceiving or forgetting being under haste
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the lexical irony of the human category, with perception or forgetting pressure now placed under the haste predicate.
topics.reason: The derivational tension survives as lexical pressure, while local syntax selects the repeated generic noun as subject of {{ar:كَانَ}} ({{tr:kāna}}).

topics.headline: human locked between being and haste
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the human noun standing between state verb and predicate, grammatically locked into the being-plus-haste frame.
topics.reason: The clause structure places {{ar:ٱلْإِنسَٰنُ}} ({{tr:al-insānu}}) between {{ar:كَانَ}} ({{tr:kāna}}) and {{ar:عَجُولًۭا}} ({{tr:ʿajūlan}}).

topics.headline: anchor for broader human diagnoses
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the generic human of 17:11 absorbs the prior group and anchors later same-surah portraits of human ungratefulness and withholding.
topics.reason: The boundary and same-surah rows give concrete discourse payoff without changing the local grammatical role.

topics.headline: human loop before final predicate
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the ayah closing its human frame just before haste lands as the answer to the whole scene.
topics.reason: The repeated noun at words 3 and 9 creates a local inclusio that prepares the final predicate.

words.gloss_range: intensive hasty or impatient predicate naming a habitual human disposition
words.root_gloss_range: haste, hurry, impatience, seeking speed, immediacy, and premature action; local faʿūl adjective selects a dispositional quality rather than a single act of hastening

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: state verb governing the final predicate

words.prose: {{ar:عَجُولًۭا}} ({{tr:ʿajūlan}}) is the accusative predicate of {{ar:كَانَ}} ({{tr:kāna}}), so haste defines the human state rather than only the moment of calling. Its faʿūl shape makes the quality intensive, habitual, and open-ended, unlike forms that would narrate seeking haste or accelerating something else. The root-family field adds premature immediacy, including the contrast between the deferred hereafter in 17:10 and desire for the immediate life at 17:18; the immaturity image remains pressure, not a literal local sense. Placed last, this rare adjectival form makes haste the diagnostic landing of the ayah, converts a motion-heavy root into a stable character label, and echoes the stronger created-from-haste image in 21:37.

topics.headline: haste as predicate, not circumstance
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that haste is the defining predicate of the human, not a passing circumstance around one act.
topics.reason: QAC and attachment evidence mark {{ar:عَجُولًۭا}} ({{tr:ʿajūlan}}) as accusative khabar of {{ar:كَانَ}} ({{tr:kāna}}).

topics.headline: habitual impatient quality
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the form diagnoses an abundant, habitual disposition rather than neutral quickness.
topics.reason: The faʿūl adjective and indefinite accusative predicate support intensive qualitative force.

topics.headline: premature immediacy pressure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that haste here means impatient orientation toward the immediate, not merely physical speed.
topics.reason: The root-family and boundary rows support immediacy and premature action; immaturity imagery is kept as root-image pressure.

topics.headline: rare faʿūl diagnosis
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that a root often seen in motion and hastening is here converted into a rare stable character label.
topics.reason: The occurrence and form rows support the contrast between other root forms and this qualitative adjective.

topics.headline: hinge to immediate-life discourse
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the final word reaching backward to the deferred hereafter in 17:10, forward to immediate-life desire in 17:18, and outward to the created-from-haste image in 21:37.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows give concrete references; they are retained as interpretive echoes while local parse remains the predicate of {{ar:كَانَ}} ({{tr:kāna}}).

topics.headline: final explanatory landing
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the last word explains the whole harm-good confusion as haste.
topics.reason: The predicate closes the diagnostic clause and the ayah, giving it final semantic prominence.

topics.headline: audible final prominence
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the final long vowel and tanwīn closure give the trait acoustic weight at the end.
topics.reason: The surface form supports a sound-level payoff at the closing word.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The comparative construction makes the human call for evil in the same manner as the call for good, then predicates haste of the human.
baseline_models.mechanism: Calling inclines an outcome toward the speaker through words; evil and beneficial good occupy the same syntactic channel, while haste advances the request before its consequences have ripened. The temporal predicate turns the confusion into a recurrent human disposition rather than an isolated slip.

activation_trace.role: Verbal calling and inclination supplies the common action applied to both opposed objects.
Evil and harm supply the negative value that the common calling mechanism fails to screen out.
Beneficial good supplies the positive value against which the harmful request is explicitly measured.
Occurrence and presence in time make haste a persisting temporal condition.
Speed and advancement before the proper time provide the mechanism that collapses evaluation into immediacy.

changed_reading.before: A person may rashly pray for something harmful just as readily as for benefit.
changed_reading.after: The ayah diagnoses a timing-driven failure of valuation: desire is verbalized before consequences mature, so one calling mechanism can misclassify harm as benefit.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The repeated call, its harmful object, and the final predicate of haste can be read as an initiating sequence.
baseline_models.mechanism: A hasty utterance is not only a mistaken wish. The call can be imaged as one fall drawing another after it, while evil is a flying spark; speed removes the interval in which the chain could be interrupted.

activation_trace.role: Successive collapse turns the call into the first link of a propagating sequence.
A flying fire-spark supplies the small released event from which wider harm can spread.
Premature speed removes the pause between ignition and propagation.

changed_reading.before: The verse reports an ill-chosen request.
changed_reading.after: The request is an initiating event: a quickly released word can spark a serial collapse whose later stages were absent from the caller's evaluation.

context_deltas.mechanism: The context repeatedly supplies shown signs, visibility, counting, and articulated detail. Because the focus inventory also lets the human root carry seeing, hearing, and sensing, haste can be read as an epistemic ordering error: petition precedes inspection and differentiation.

activation_trace.role: Perceiving by sight, hearing, or inward sensing makes the human agent an evaluator, not merely a desiring body.
Advancement before the proper time places the request ahead of adequate perception.
Causing something to be seen supplies disclosure as the prerequisite the hasty caller bypasses.
A manifest sign supplies observable evidence against which good and evil could be distinguished.
Visual apprehension makes the day-side of the sequence a field for informed seeking.
Counting and reckoning supply the temporal calculation missing from premature desire.
Detailing parts and meanings supplies the discriminating operation that haste compresses.

structural_cues: The opening movement is ordered toward being shown signs, while 17:12 makes alternating night and day serve seeking, counting, and detailed articulation.
The focus sits between a warning about a deferred outcome and a verse devoted to temporal visibility and calculation.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies perception, signs, reckoning, detail, and the focus predicate of haste; I infer the arrow from insufficient inspection to misvalued petition. A live alternative is that these signs orient conduct generally without describing the cognition behind the focus call.

changed_reading.before: Haste is mainly excessive speed in wanting.
changed_reading.after: Haste is also a sequence error in knowing: the human calls before seeing, counting, and separating enough to tell apparent good from actual harm.

context_deltas.mechanism: The earlier context turns isolated action into recurrence: an event happens twice, advantage is returned, the turn recurs, and good or harm is directed to the same self before the formula 'if you return, We return.' The focus call therefore enters a reflexive cycle rather than departing harmlessly from the speaker.

activation_trace.role: One stage falling after another supplies the focus-side propagation that recurrence amplifies.
A temporal occurrence and repetition establish that the surrounding mechanism is iterative.
Return to a prior position supplies the reversal by which an apparent endpoint becomes another beginning.
Return and reiteration after a first occurrence make recurrence explicit.
Doing good supplies the positive action whose benefit is grammatically redirected to its agents.
The very self or entity supplies the receiver to whom both sides of the moral contrast return.
What causes hurt supplies the negative action and effect redirected toward that same self.
Return after departure, repeated in both condition and answer, closes the feedback loop.

structural_cues: The sequence moves from 'twice' in 17:4 through returned advantage in 17:6 to matched good and harm in 17:7 and the doubled return formula in 17:8.
The parallel clauses in 17:7 give positive and negative action the same self-directed grammar, echoing the focus comparison between calling for evil and calling for good.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies recurrence, reversal, and self-directed moral symmetry; I infer that the focus utterance participates in that feedback structure. The live alternative is that 17:4-8 remains a collective historical cycle and does not specify the causal path of each individual call.

changed_reading.before: A hasty utterance can start a one-way harmful chain.
changed_reading.after: The utterance is dangerous because the chain is recursive and reflexive: what is called and enacted can return through repeated turns to the same human who misnamed it as good.

context_deltas.mechanism: Immediately before the focus, the context gives good a procedural test: gentle direction toward a path, upright alignment, fitting action, and resulting recompense. This revises 'good' from whatever attracts a request into a criterion that desire must answer to.

activation_trace.role: Verbal inclination supplies the desire-driven motion whose object needs an external criterion.
Choosing and seeking the better option pose the question of how the caller identifies what is actually good.
Gentle indication toward the right path supplies a criterion beyond immediate attraction.
Straightness, balance, and uprightness define the alignment by which a desired object can be tested.
Purposive work shifts the positive course from wish alone to enacted pursuit.
Fitness and suitability supply a relational test for whether an action truly belongs to the good.
Recompense after work supplies an outcome structurally different from immediate acquisition.

structural_cues: The clause sequence in 17:9 moves from guidance to the most upright course, then to belief, fitting work, and recompense.
The focus follows after 17:10 adds the deferred horizon that some agents reject.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies a guided and enacted path adjacent to the focus; I infer that it functions as the test the hasty caller omits when naming an object good. A live alternative is that 17:9 promises an outcome without defining the focus term 'good.'

changed_reading.before: Good is the beneficial object the human intends to request.
changed_reading.after: Good is not secured by intensity of wanting; it is a guided, upright, fitting course with an outcome, while haste substitutes attraction for that criterion.

context_deltas.mechanism: The context names rejection of the later horizon just before the focus, then reuses the haste root for desiring 'the immediate' and contrasts it with willing the later horizon through its due striving. Haste is therefore not only tempo but a horizon-selection rule that rates fast arrival above terminal consequence.

activation_trace.role: Calling and verbal inclination provide the act whose object is selected under a temporal horizon.
Speed and advancement before due time provide the focus diagnosis that the later context lexicalizes.
Deferral to a later time supplies the horizon excluded immediately before the focus.
Painful punishment supplies the delayed negative consequence absent from an immediate valuation.
The immediate object and its acceleration make the focus predicate into an explicit temporal economy.
Will and intention distinguish the human demand for immediacy from the selective will governing what is accelerated.
Encounter with fire supplies the terminal consequence hidden by the near-term object.
The later horizon supplies the explicit counterpart to the immediate.
Purposeful motion toward a sought end replaces instant petition with sustained trajectory.
Acknowledged and commended effort supplies the positive valuation reached at the end of the deferred path.

structural_cues: The focus is immediately preceded by nonbelief in the later horizon and its painful consequence.
Verses 17:18-19 form parallel conditional alternatives: desire for the immediate and accelerated allotment versus desire for the later horizon and its corresponding striving.
The repeated haste root in 17:18 is the clearest lexical return to the focus predicate.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the immediate/later contrast, repeated haste root, selective acceleration, and purposeful striving; I infer that arrival speed is the hidden metric by which the focus human mistakes evil for good. A live alternative is that the focus haste describes rash speech more narrowly, while 17:18 classifies life aims.

changed_reading.before: The human is impulsive within a single request.
changed_reading.after: The human adopts immediacy as a value horizon: what arrives quickly is treated as good even when its terminal path is harmful, whereas the later good requires sustained directed effort.

context_deltas.mechanism: The context converts what appears transient into what adheres, is written, spread open, read, and reckoned by the self. Applied to the focus, a hasty call does not vanish when voiced; it becomes inspectable material within the caller's own account.

activation_trace.role: Voiced calling supplies the apparently transient event that the context refigures as durable evidence.
Affixing something by obligation makes consequence inseparable from its human bearer.
Joined letters and the written object supply durable, legible form.
The spread-open writing supplies later exposure of what had seemed finished.
Reading and recitation turn the durable trace back into addressed language.
The self as the thing itself supplies both bearer and witness of the trace.
Counting and accounting supply the evaluative return of the recorded act.

structural_cues: Verses 17:13-14 move in sequence from attachment to a book, its open presentation, an imperative to read, and self-accounting.
The repeated human noun links the focus agent directly to the bearer of the attached account.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies attachment, book, opening, reading, and self-reckoning; I infer that the focus call belongs among the acts made durable. A live alternative is that the book covers deeds broadly and the packet does not isolate petitions as its entries.

changed_reading.before: The hasty call is a fleeting verbal mistake.
changed_reading.after: The call can be carried as durable self-evidence: speech released too soon remains attached, becomes legible, and returns to the speaker as an object of reckoning.

context_deltas.mechanism: A later civic sequence supplies a scaled-up cascade: abundance releases its possessors, they breach a containing boundary, the uttered determination becomes binding, and demolition follows. This activates the focus call as a social trigger-chain in which what feels like available good can loosen restraint and mature into collective harm.

activation_trace.role: Successive falling provides the focus-side template for a multi-stage collapse.
A released spark supplies the small ignition that can become systemic damage.
Expansive luxury that releases its possessor supplies the permissive pressure at the start of the civic chain.
A ripe date exiting its peel supplies a concrete image of actors breaching containment.
Binding necessity supplies the transition from breach to an outcome that has become due.
An uttered saying supplies the speech-event that is realized within the chain.
Root-and-branch destruction supplies the terminal state of the propagated sequence.

structural_cues: Verse 17:16 is a tightly linked verbal chain: intention, command, affluent transgression, the word becoming due, and repeated-form destruction.
The focus itself places the call before the characterization of haste, allowing speech to be tested as an initiating act.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies a city-scale causal sequence and focus branches of cascading fall and spark; I map that sequence onto the individual call as a possible social amplification path. The materially live alternative is that 17:16 concerns collective judgment only and does not explain how a petition causes harm.

changed_reading.before: A rash request primarily endangers the individual caller.
changed_reading.after: Exploratorily, the call can model a civic ignition: desired abundance releases restraint, boundary breach makes a word binding, and the resulting evil propagates beyond the original caller.

context_deltas.mechanism: The closing context weakens any simple claim that calling mechanically produces its object. Both temporal orientations receive continuing extension from a gift not barred, while recipients and later degrees remain differentiated. The focus call operates inside a larger allocation rather than functioning as an executable command.

activation_trace.role: Calling supplies the petition whose causal authority is being qualified.
Connected increase that supports another supplies an ongoing source beyond the caller's utterance.
Giving and handing over place receipt on the donor side rather than under unilateral human control.
The negated image of prohibition marks the breadth of giving without making every request determinative.
Rank and excellence supply qualitative differentiation within what is given.
Partition into portions prevents the field of recipients from collapsing into one undifferentiated outcome.
Stepwise degrees supply an ordered scale that immediate yes-or-no petition does not capture.

structural_cues: Verse 17:20 repeats 'these and these' under one source of extension, then denies that the gift is barred.
Verse 17:21 immediately commands comparison and describes differential degrees.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies continued giving to both groups and differentiated degrees; I infer that petition is not a sufficient cause of allotment. A live alternative is that broad giving and effective prayer coexist, so the context may qualify only the caller's control rather than the call's efficacy.

changed_reading.before: The hasty call itself sets the harmful outcome in motion.
changed_reading.after: That causal reading must be qualified: the call reveals misvaluation and may initiate conduct, but receipt remains part of a broader, graded distribution not commanded by the utterance.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it uses the split mapped root's image of shaking a measure and the rare image of setting something down before its vessel as a material analogy for prayer. It remains anchored in the repeated call and final haste predicate, whose branches explicitly supply those operations. Downstream prose should mark it as a container-and-capacity model, not as the lexical meaning of the ayah.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The repeated call supplies the forcing motion, while the final haste term supplies a premature order of placement.

activation_trace.role: Shaking a measure or vessel until it packs full supplies the image of demand forcing immediate capacity.
Putting something down before its vessel supplies the exact material reversal of receiving before readiness.
Beneficial good supplies the quality criterion displaced when filling now becomes the sole objective.

changed_reading.before: The caller asks too quickly for a wrongly valued object.
changed_reading.after: The caller tries to shake reality full and receive before a fitting vessel exists; evil and good collapse into the single metric of immediate filling.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it activates exchange and equivalence branches from the non-dominant mapped root behind the focus evil root. It remains anchored in the explicit comparison between evil and good and in the branch-resolved split supplied by the packet. Downstream prose should present it as an economic analogy for evaluative error, never as a replacement translation of the evil term.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The focus places evil and good in a grammatical comparison under the same repeated calling act.

activation_trace.role: Exchange between buying and selling supplies a transaction model for how the caller takes harm as a desired return.
Matching and equivalence supply the mispricing operation implicit in treating evil like good.
Choosing the better option supplies the valuation decision that the hasty exchange gets wrong.
Premature advancement explains why equivalence is accepted before long-term value is known.

changed_reading.before: The human confuses two opposed objects of prayer.
changed_reading.after: The human performs a rushed valuation exchange, accepting harm as though it were an equivalent return for good.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it joins a branch image of sharp, unrestrained flight to the neck-bound object and open book in 17:13. It remains anchored in the focus's voiced call and haste, and the context explicitly binds, locates, and unfolds the flying object. Downstream prose should qualify this as a material metaphor for released speech and accountability; the packet does not state that the attached bird is specifically a spoken petition.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: A hasty voiced call can be imaged as leaving quickly, while the following human-centered scene denies that what leaves is thereby detached.

activation_trace.role: Voiced calling supplies the speech-event that appears to leave the speaker.
Rapid advancement supplies the release velocity of the utterance.
Sharp, rash, unbound motion supplies the flight-image for speech sent out before reflection.
Affixing by obligation reverses the apparent escape of the flying act.
The neck supplies a bodily point of attachment to the same human agent.
A written object spread open supplies eventual exposure of the once-flying act.

changed_reading.before: The hasty word departs and its danger lies only in what it immediately triggers.
changed_reading.after: The word flies out but does not escape its speaker: it remains tethered to the human and can later be unfolded as accountable trace.

strongest_changes: The return sequence in 17:4-8 turns a one-way hasty utterance into a recursive, self-directed consequence.
The immediate-versus-later contrast in 17:10 and 17:18-19 makes haste a value horizon that mistakes speed of arrival for goodness.
Shown signs, temporal reckoning, and the attached open account make the focus error both epistemically premature and durably inspectable.
summary.what_was_special: The context reuses the focus human and haste roots while surrounding them with recurrence, visibility, accounting, selective acceleration, and graded giving. Split root inventories also preserve material models of forced filling and mispriced exchange without requiring those models to displace the direct moral reading.
remaining_uncertainties: The focus call may be literal petition, curse, wish, or a broader class of impulsive speech.
The transfer from collective recurrence and civic destruction to an individual call remains abductive.
The split-root container, exchange, and flight images are branch-resolved but should bear less interpretive weight than the direct temporal recurrence.

reader_a.activated_readings_md: 1. **Haste erases the discrimination built into calling.** `د ع و:B001/B004` spans calling near and calling down harm, `خ ي ر:B003` choosing the better option, and `ع ج ل:B001/B005` haste and hurried provision. Identical *duʿāʾ* syntax holds evil and good in the same slot; 17:18–21 later contrasts the hurried with differentiated degrees. I infer temporal compression prevents evaluation, making opposed outcomes feel equally callable. The ayah reads haste as a cognitive mechanism that mislabels harm as benefit.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 17:100 gives the economic form of the same haste-error: fear of future outflow makes humans withhold even imagined inexhaustible mercy. Projected futures distort present action in both ayat.

reader_a.activated_readings_md: 1. **Hasty prayer as pulling an adverse future forward.** Lexical evidence: `د ع و B004` (calling down an unwelcome thing) in `يَدْعُ ... بِٱلشَّرِّ`, and `ع ج ل B001` (hastening and bringing forward) in `عَجُولًا`. Structural cue: 17:8 makes return elicit return, 17:10 says punishment is prepared, and 17:12–14 orders time, count, and reckoning. Assigned role: invocation draws a possible outcome near; haste collapses the interval needed to distinguish it from good. Abductive move: the packet supplies the call and temporal impatience; I infer that haste causes the caller to solicit prematurely what an ordered reckoning would expose as harmful. Reading change: the ayah diagnoses not mere verbal inconsistency but a causal misuse of prayer that attempts to accelerate an adverse future.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 17:12 corrected the first impression most strongly: its measured night/day cycle shows that `عَجُولًا` collapses an interval designed for discrimination and حساب.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_channel: P1 (17:1-22): Desire, Effort, and Apportioned Outcome
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_semantic_invariant: An inward aim becomes motion and work, while the eventual share is extended, limited, or ranked by an allocator beyond the worker.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_surprising_reach: Desire appears as bodily haste and route choice, striving carries an emancipation sense, and allotment behaves like a connected supply distributed by degree.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: The Hasty Call That Misnames Harm as Good
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: Speech draws an object toward the caller before discernment has separated benefit from injury.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: vocal summons (`quranic:root_000478:B001/m01`); invocation of descending harm (`quranic:root_000478:B004/m01`); injurious evil (`quranic:root_000787:B001/m01`); beneficial good (`quranic:root_000452:B001/m01`); acceleration and premature advance (`quranic:root_000987:B001/m01`); provision demanded in advance (`quranic:root_000987:B005/m01`)
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: The call is causative: it seeks to pull an outcome near. Haste collapses the distinction between good and harm, and the latent image of advance provision makes the error one of demanding receipt before value has been judged.

neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Odak dal kalanın amacıyla tanımlanır; komşu dal ise miktarın azlığıyla tanımlanır ve sonraki sütü çekme işlevini gerektirmez.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Süt akışını uyarmak için memede bırakılan sütün kendisini adlandırır.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Memeyi sıvazlayarak sütü indirme eylemini ve bu yolla süt veren hayvanı kapsar.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: İki dal da memeden yeni süt akışını başlatma veya sürdürme amacı taşır.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Bu dalda uyarıcı araç memede bırakılan süt payıdır; komşuda araç memenin sıvazlanmasıdır.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Bir miktar sütü sonraki akışı sağlamak üzere memede bırakmayı anlatır.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Parmak uçlarıyla az az sağmayı, yavaş akışı ve kalan sütü çekip almayı kapsar.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Her iki dal da memedeki az miktardaki süt ve sağımın sürdürülmesi alanındadır.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Odak dal sütü bırakır ve işlevini bekler; komşu dal az miktardaki sütü belirli bir sağım biçimiyle dışarı alır.

branches.neighbor_coverage_note: Adayların tamamı incelendi. Seçilen komşular, amaçlı bırakılan süt payını az süt kalıntısından, memeyi sıvazlamaktan ve az az sağmaktan ayırır; öteki adaylar sağımın başka aşamalarına veya kardeş anlamlara aittir.

identity_judgment.rationale: Hazırlanan çerçeve bunu birine kötülük gelmesi için söz söyleme olarak sunarken kaynak ifadesi, Tanrı'nın kişinin başına hoşlanmadığı şeyi getirmesini ve olayın gerçekleşmesini anlatır. Dal korunabilir, ancak tanım sözlü dilekten gerçekleşen sıkıntıya kaydırılmalıdır.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Anlam, belirli yapıda Tanrı'nın istenmeyen bir şeyi kişinin başına getirmesidir; kötülük dileme eylemi değildir.

lexicalization_scope.note: Düzeltilen anlam yalnızca verilen Tanrı, kişi ve istenmeyen sonuç yapısında geçerlidir; yalın çağırma anlamına genellenmez.

concept_map.definition: Belirli yapıda, Tanrı'nın bir kişinin başına onun hoşlanmadığı bir sıkıntıyı getirmesini anlatır. Odak, birinin kötülük dilemesi değil, istenmeyen olayın kişiye yönelip gerçekleşmesidir.

facets.statement: Tanrı, kişiye onun hoşlanmadığı bir şeyi yöneltir ve başına getirir.
Kaynak açıklaması sözlü bir kötülük isteğini değil, istenmeyen sonucun kişide gerçekleşmesini öne çıkarır.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Tek kaynak iddiası, Tanrı'nın bir kişiye hoşlanmadığı şeyi indirmesi veya başına getirmesi sonucunu bildirir; sözlü bir kötülük dileme işlemi belirtmez.

concept_gloss.text: Tanrı'nın birine istemediği bir sıkıntıyı vermesi
concept_gloss.applicability: Tanrı'nın bir kişinin başına o kişinin hoşlanmadığı bir olay veya sıkıntı getirdiğini bildiren özel yapı için uygundur.

error_profile.preserves: Eyleyenin Tanrı olmasını, etkilenen kişiyi ve onun istemediği sonucun gerçekleşmesini korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Eyleyeni geri planda bırakıp kişi açısından gerçekleşen istenmeyen sonucu anlatmak gerektiğinde kullanılabilir.

error_profile.preserves: Kişinin başına hoşlanmadığı bir sıkıntının gelmesi sonucunu korur.
error_profile.loses: Sonucu Tanrı'nın meydana getirdiğini açıkça belirtmez.

lexical_glosses.target_gloss: Tanrı'nın birinin başına hoşlanmadığı bir sıkıntıyı getirmesi

error_profile.preserves: Bir kişiye yönelen istenmeyen sonuç düşüncesini korur.
error_profile.loses: Kaynakta bildirilen gerçekleşmiş ilahi yöneltme ve meydana gelme ilişkisini kaybeder.
error_profile.adds: Bir insanın sözlü istekte bulunduğu ayrı bir konuşma eylemi ekler.
error_profile.collision: Sonucun gerçekleşmesini, o sonucun gerçekleşmesini isteme eylemiyle karıştırır.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Tanrı'nın istenmeyen şeyi kişinin başına getirmesi ve sonucun gerçekleşmesi anlatılır.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Bir kişinin başkasına kötülük yönelten söz söylemesi öne çıkar.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Her iki dal da belirli bir kişinin başına kötü bir şey gelmesi düşüncesini taşır.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Odak dal gerçekleşen ilahi yöneltmeyi bildirir; komşu dal ise kötü sonucun gerçekleşmesi için söylenen sözü anlatır.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: İstenmeyen sonucun Tanrı tarafından kişiye verilmesini bildirir.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Lanetleme ve karşılıklı olarak yalancının cezalandırılmasını isteme törenlerini kapsar.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: İki dal da Tanrı ile ilişkilendirilen kötü bir sonucun kişiye yönelmesi sahnesini paylaşır.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Bu dal sonuç bildiren özel bir yapıdır; komşu dal sözlü lanetleme veya karşılıklı sınama eylemidir.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Sıkıntının belirli bir eyleyen tarafından kişiye getirilmesi ilişkisini içerir.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Sıkıntı, zarar veya güçlüğün kendisini ve onun yoğunluğunu anlatır.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Her iki dal da kişinin yaşadığı hoş olmayan ve zarar verici durumu kapsar.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Odak dal sıkıntının kişiye yöneltilmesini anlatır; komşu dal yönelten bir eyleyen gerektirmeden sıkıntı durumunu adlandırır.

branches.neighbor_coverage_note: Bütün adaylar karşılaştırıldı. Seçilenler gerçekleşen sıkıntıyı kötülük dileme, lanetleme ve sıkıntının kendisinden ayırır; kalanlar uzak sonuç türleri veya bu kökün başka dallarıdır.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi iki bağlı süreci açıkça verir: duvarların birbiri ardından çökmesi ve yapıların birbiri ardından yıkılması. Hazırlanan çerçeve, ardışıklığı ve çökme ile ettirgen yıkma ayrımını korur.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Birbiri ardından gerçekleşme her iki kullanımda da kurucudur; tek bir çökme veya tek seferde yıkma dalın tamamını karşılamaz.

lexicalization_scope.note: Kendiliğinden ardışık çöküş ile bir eyleyenin ardışık yıkması ayrı yapılara bağlı iki facet olarak korunur.

concept_map.definition: Bir yapının parçalarının birbiri ardından çökmesi veya bir eyleyenin onları birbiri ardından yıkmasıdır. Her iki durumda da tek olay değil, birbirini izleyen bir bozulma dizisi vardır.

facets.statement: Yapısal bozulma tek seferde değil, parçaların birbirini izlemesiyle gerçekleşir.
Duvarlar veya yapı parçaları kendiliğinden birbiri ardından çöker.
Bir eyleyen, yapı parçalarını hedefin üzerine birbiri ardından yıkar.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Tek iddia, ardışık çöküşü ve ardışık ettirgen yıkmayı aynı sıra ilişkisi altında birleştirir; eyleyenin bulunup bulunmaması iki kullanımı ayırır.

concept_gloss.applicability: Hem yapı parçalarının sırayla çökmesini hem de bir eyleyenin onları sırayla yıkmasını kapsayan üst karşılıktır.

error_profile.preserves: Ardışıklığı, yapısal bozulmayı ve kendiliğinden çökme ile ettirgen yıkma seçeneklerini korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Duvar veya yapı parçalarının kendiliğinden ve sırayla düştüğü kullanım için doğaldır.

error_profile.preserves: Yapı parçalarının ardışık biçimde çökmesini korur.
error_profile.loses: Bir eyleyenin parçaları birbiri ardından yıkması kullanımını kapsamaz.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Bir eyleyenin yapı parçalarını hedefin üzerine sırayla yıktığı kullanım için uygundur.

error_profile.preserves: Ettirgen yıkmayı ve parçaların sıra ile devrilmesini korur.
error_profile.loses: Yapının kendiliğinden ardışık çökmesi kullanımını kapsamaz.

error_profile.preserves: Yapının ayakta kalma durumunu yitirerek düşmesini korur.
error_profile.loses: Parçaların birbiri ardından gelmesini ve ettirgen yıkma kullanımını kaybeder.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Çöküşün veya yıkmanın parçalar arasında sıra halinde ilerlemesini ve ettirgen seçeneği kapsar.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Bir şeyin genel olarak düşmesi veya yıkılmasını, ayrıca ağacın kökünden çıkmasını kapsar.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Her iki dal da bir yapının ayakta kalma durumunu yitirip çökmesini anlatır.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Odak dal için ardışıklık kurucudur; komşu dal tek bir çöküşü de kapsar ve sıra ilişkisi gerektirmez.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Birbiri ardından çökme veya yıkma düzenini vurgular.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Yıkılmanın taşıyıcı düzeni, gücü veya itibarı ortadan kaldıran sonucunu da kapsar.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: İki dal da yapıların yıkılması ve ayakta tutan düzenin bozulması alanında örtüşür.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Bu dal olayların sırasıyla tanımlanır; komşu dal ise yıkımın dayanıklılığı ve düzeni yok eden sonucuyla tanımlanır.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Birden çok parçanın birbirini izleyerek çökmesini veya yıkılmasını gerektirir.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Bir yapının ya da kenarın yüksekten aşağıya veya çukura doğru çöküş yönünü öne çıkarır.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Her iki dal da yapı parçalarının düşmesi ve bütünlüğün bozulması olayını kapsar.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Odak dalın ayırıcı özelliği ardışık sıra, komşunun ayırıcı özelliği ise aşağıya veya derine doğru çöküş yönüdür.

branches.neighbor_coverage_note: Tüm adaylar değerlendirildi. Yayınlanan komşular ardışıklık sınırını genel çökme, sonucu öne çıkan yıkım ve aşağı yönlü çöküşten ayırır; kalan adaylar kırma, zayıflama, düzleme veya kardeş anlam alanlarında daha uzaktır.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi dönemin değişimlerini ve olayların yönünü değiştirmelerini anlatır. Hazırlanan çerçevenin olaylar ve yön verme bölümü uygundur, ancak insanın bu olaylara eğilmesi kaynakta kurucu bir katılımcı olarak açıkça verilmez.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Tanım, insanın yönelmesini değil, dönemin olayların akışını başka yöne çeviren değişimlerini merkeze alır.

lexicalization_scope.note: Anlam yalnızca dönemin yön verici değişimleri yapısına bağlıdır; yalın biçime genel bir olay veya çağırma anlamı yüklenmez.

concept_map.definition: Dönemin olayların akışını başka yöne çeviren değişimleri ve getirdiği gelişmelerdir. Yöneltme düşüncesi burada sesli bir çağrı değil, olayların seyrine etki eden mecazlı bir güçtür.

facets.statement: Dönem, değişen koşullar ve gelişmeler yoluyla olayların akışına yön verir.
Olayların başka yöne çevrilmesi, temel yöneltme ilişkisini zamansal değişimlere taşıyan mecazlı bir uzantıdır.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Tek iddia, dönemin değişimlerini olayların yönünü etkileyen güçler olarak sunar; insanın bu değişimlere çekilmesi kaynak ifadesinde zorunlu bir öğe değildir.

concept_gloss.applicability: Dönemin getirdiği değişimlerin olayların seyrini etkilediğini anlatan özel kullanım için uygundur.

error_profile.preserves: Dönemin değişimlerini, olayları ve bu değişimlerin yön verici etkisini birlikte korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Yön verme benzetisini açmadan, dönem içinde meydana gelen değişim ve gelişmeleri doğal Türkçeyle anlatır.

error_profile.preserves: Dönemin değişkenliğini ve onunla birlikte ortaya çıkan olayları korur.
error_profile.loses: Bu değişimlerin olayların yönünü çevirdiği mecazlı ilişkiyi açıkça göstermez.

error_profile.preserves: Olayların yön verici bir etkisi olduğu düşüncesini korur.
error_profile.loses: Dönemin değişimleri ile olayların seyrinin yön değiştirmesi arasındaki bağı zayıflatır.
error_profile.adds: Kaynakta kurucu olmayan insan katılımcısını ve onun edilgin biçimde sürüklenmesini ekler.
error_profile.collision: Olayların yönünün değişmesi ile insanın olaylara kapılması birbirine karışır.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Dönemin değişimlerini olayların yönünü etkileyen bir güç olarak kavramlaştırır.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Dönemin insanlar üzerinde gerçekleşen türlü olaylarını ve bazı kullanımlarda gece ile gündüzü de kapsar.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Her iki dal da dönem içinde ortaya çıkan değişimleri ve olayların değişken seyrini anlatır.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Odak dal yön verme benzetisiyle sınırlıdır; komşu dal daha genel olayları ve daha geniş zamansal kullanımları kapsar.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Değişimleri, olumlu veya olumsuz değer yüklemeden olayların yönünü değiştirmeleri bakımından ele alır.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Beklenen veya korkulan uğursuz gelişmeler ve belirsizlik duygusunu öne çıkarır.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: İki dal da dönemin getirdiği değişimleri ve beklenmedik gelişmeleri kapsar.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Bu dal genel yön değişimini anlatır; komşu dal değişimlerin kaygı, kuşku ve kötü beklenti doğuran yönüyle sınırlıdır.

branches.neighbor_coverage_note: Adayların tümü karşılaştırıldı. İki yakın komşu, yön verici dönem değişimini genel dönem olaylarından ve kaygı uyandıran gelişmelerden ayırır; diğer adaylar ölüm, insanın durumu, yaklaşan sonuç veya kardeş anlamlarla daha dolaylı ilişkilidir.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi, gizlenmiş cevabı ortaya çıkarmak için karşılıklı olarak sorulan bilmece türü soruları ve birine böyle bir soru yöneltme eylemini birlikte verir. Hazırlanan çerçeve bu soru, gizleme ve cevap çıkarma ilişkisini korur.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Dal sıradan anlaşılmaz sözü değil, gizlenmiş bir cevabı buldurmak üzere yöneltilen bilmece ve sınama eylemini kapsar.

lexicalization_scope.note: Bilmece olarak kullanılan adlandırma ile birine bilmece yöneltme eylemi ayrı facetlerde korunur; anlam genel seslenmeye yayılmaz.

concept_map.definition: Gizlenmiş bir cevabı ortaya çıkarmak için birine yöneltilen bilmece türü soru veya böyle sorularla karşılıklı sınamadır. Soru, muhatabı örtülü cevabı bulup söylemeye çağırır.

facets.statement: Soru, cevabı doğrudan vermeyip onu örtülü ve çözülmesi gereken halde sunar.
Kişiler bu tür soruları birbirlerine yönelterek karşılıklı bir sınama yürütür.
Eylem biçimi, muhataba bir bilmece sunup gizli cevabı ondan istemeyi anlatır.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Tek iddia, bilmece niteliğindeki örtülü soruyu, bu sorularla karşılıklı sınamayı ve muhataptan gizli cevabı çıkarma amacını birlikte temellendirir.

concept_gloss.applicability: Örtülü bir cevabı ortaya çıkarmak için kişilerin birbirine bilmece türü soru yönelttiği kavramı karşılar.

error_profile.preserves: Gizli cevabı, onu buldurma amacını, bilmece biçimini ve karşılıklı sınamayı korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Bir kişinin muhatabına örtülü cevabı bulması için soru yönelttiği eylem bağlamında doğaldır.

error_profile.preserves: Birine çözülmesi gereken örtülü bir soru yöneltme eylemini korur.
error_profile.loses: Soruların karşılıklı yürütülmesini ve cevabı özellikle ortaya çıkarma benzetisini tek başına göstermez.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Kişilerin birbirine örtülü sorular yönelterek cevap verme gücünü denediği bağlamlarda kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Karşılıklılığı, bilmece biçimini ve sınama işlevini korur.
error_profile.loses: Gizlenmiş cevabı muhataptan ortaya çıkarma yönünü açıkça söylemez.

lexical_glosses.target_gloss: gizli cevabı buldurmak için karşılıklı sorulan bilmeceler

error_profile.preserves: İçeriğin hemen anlaşılmaması ve çözüm gerektirmesi yönünü kısmen korur.
error_profile.loses: Soru biçimini, gizli cevabı buldurma amacını ve karşılıklı sınamayı kaybeder.
error_profile.adds: Cevabı olmayan her türlü belirsiz veya bozuk sözü kapsayabilir.
error_profile.collision: Amaçlı bilmeceyi rastgele anlaşılmaz anlatımla karıştırır.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Örtülü soruyu bir muhataba yöneltir ve ondan gizli cevabı ortaya çıkarmasını ister.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Sözü veya nesneyi genel olarak anlaşılması güç hale getirmeyi, soru ve cevap düzeni aramadan kapsar.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Her iki dal da anlamı hemen erişilemez kılan örtme ve çözme gereksinimini taşır.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Odak dal amaçlı bir bilmece ve cevap isteme eylemidir; komşu dal daha geniş biçimde sözü anlaşılmazlaştırmayı anlatır.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Muhatabı güç bir soruyla cevap vermeye ve örtülü çözümü bulmaya yöneltir.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Kişinin cevap bulamadığı veya sözü tükendiği için susmasını anlatır.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: İki dal, zor bir söz karşısında cevap verme veya cevap verememe sahnesinde birleşir.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Bu dal soruyu yönelten sınama eylemidir; komşu dal ise sınanan kişinin cevapsız kalmasının sonucudur.

branches.neighbor_coverage_note: Tüm adaylar incelendi. Seçilen iki komşu bilmeceyi genel anlaşılmazlaştırmadan ve cevapsız kalma sonucundan ayırır; kalan adaylar doğrulama, bilgi, çelişki, karşı koyma veya kardeş anlamlarla yalnızca uzak bağ taşır.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi, belirli bir ev yapısında hiç kimsenin bulunmadığını, seslenebilecek tek bir kişinin bile olmaması üzerinden açıklar. Hazırlanan dal çerçevesi hem yokluk sonucunu hem de ses veren kimse benzetisini korur.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Anlam belirli olumsuz ev ifadesine bağlıdır ve genel olarak boşluk, sessizlik veya eşyasızlık bildirmez.

lexicalization_scope.note: Hiç kimsenin bulunmadığı anlamı yalnızca verilen kalıplaşmış olumsuz yapıda geçerlidir; yalın biçime taşınmaz.

concept_map.definition: Belirli bir olumsuz ev ifadesinde, içeride hiç kimsenin bulunmadığını bildirir. Açıklayıcı benzetme, seslenip bağıracak tek bir kişinin bile olmayışıdır.

facets.statement: Belirtilen evde hiçbir insan bulunmaz.
İnsan yokluğu, evde seslenebilecek veya bağırabilecek kimsenin bulunmamasıyla açıklanır.

concept_gloss.applicability: Belirli yapının bir evde tek bir insanın bile bulunmadığını bildiren tam anlamı için uygundur.

error_profile.preserves: Ev sınırını, insan yokluğunu ve yokluğun eksiksiz oluşunu korur.

error_profile.loses: Seslenip bağıracak birinin bile olmayışı üzerinden kurulan açıklayıcı benzetiyi göstermez.

error_profile.preserves: Evde insan bulunmaması olasılığını ve genel yokluk düşüncesini korur.
error_profile.loses: İfadenin yalnızca insan bulunmadığını kesin biçimde bildiren sınırını kaybeder.

neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Her iki dal da kalıplaşmış olumsuz bir ev ifadesiyle içeride tek bir kişinin bile bulunmadığını bildirir.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Kavramsal çekirdek ve sınır aynıdır; ayrım yalnızca bu anlamı taşıyan kalıplaşmış sözlerin farklı oluşudur.

neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: İki dal da belirli bir evde hiçbir insan bulunmadığını kalıplaşmış olumsuz sözle anlatır.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Anlam ve kullanım sınırı örtüşür; yalnızca insan yokluğunu anlatmak için seçilen sözlü görüntü farklıdır.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: İnsan yokluğunu evle sınırlı özel bir ifade ve seslenebilecek kimse benzetisiyle kurar.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: İnsan yokluğunu ev dışındaki bir yer için de kullanılabilen başka bir dar ifadeyle bildirir.

neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Odak dal ev ve seslenen kişi görüntüsüne bağlıdır; komşu dalın yer sınırı daha geneldir ve aynı açıklayıcı görüntüyü taşımaz.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Belirli bir evde insan bulunmamasını ses verecek kimsenin yokluğuyla açıklar.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Bir yerde hiç kimse veya hiçbir belirti bulunmamasını daha geniş bir yokluk alanında kapsayabilir.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: İki dal da bir mekanın insanlardan yoksun oluşunu kalıplaşmış olumsuz ifadelerle bildirir.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Bu dal yalnızca evde insan yokluğudur; komşu dal yer sınırını genişletir ve insan dışında belirti yokluğuna da uzanabilir.

identity_judgment.rationale: Yetkili kaynak ifadesi itme eyleminde birleşir; ancak sertlik, kabalık ve azarlama niteliği bütün aktarımlarda aynı ölçüde kurucu değildir. Bu yüzden dal, sıradan itme çekirdeğini koruyup sert ve kaba gerçekleşmeleri belirgin kullanımlar olarak ayırmalıdır.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Çekirdek fiziksel itmedir; sertlik ve azarlama bazı kullanımları daraltır, doldurma veya seslenme anlamları bu dala girmez.

lexicalization_scope.note: Tanım çıplak itme çekirdeğiyle yapıya bağlı sertçe sürme ve azarlama örneklerini ayırır; özel yapılar bütün dalın anlamı sayılmaz.

concept_map.definition: Birini ya da bir şeyi itmek; belirli kullanımlarda bunu sertçe, kaba davranarak veya azarlayıcı biçimde yapmaktır.

facets.statement: Bir varlığı bulunduğu yerden fiziksel güçle itme eylemidir.
Eylem sertlik, kabalık ve azarlama eşliğinde gerçekleşebilir.
Bazı yapılarda savunmasız birini itip azarlamayı veya bir yere zorla sürmeyi anlatır.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Aktarımlar itme çekirdeğinde birleşir; bir bölümü eylemin sert, kaba ve azarlayıcı niteliğini ayrıca öne çıkarır.

error_profile.preserves: Fiziksel güçle yerinden oynatma çekirdeğini tam olarak korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Sertliğin veya kaba davranışın açıkça öne çıktığı bağlamlarda doğal karşılıktır.

error_profile.preserves: Hem itme eylemini hem de eylemin sert gerçekleşmesini korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Birinin belirli bir yöne veya yere şiddetle sevk edildiği yapılarda kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Zorlayıcı güç ve yönlü hareket özelliklerini korur.
error_profile.loses: Yön belirtmeyen yalın itme kullanımlarını kapsamaz.

error_profile.adds: Temasın sürmesi ve nesnenin çekilmesi anlamını ekler.
error_profile.collision: Türkçede çekerek ilerletme eylemiyle karışır.

identity_judgment.rationale: Yetkili kaynak ifadesi, bir ölçek kabını veya başka bir taşıyıcıyı hareket ettirerek içindekini yerleştirme ve kabı dolu ya da sıkışık duruma getirme sürecini açıkça destekler. Sonuç bildiren doldurma kullanımları aynı işlemin doğal uzantısıdır.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Ayırıcı özellik yalnızca doluluk değil, kabı hareket ettirerek kapasitesini kullanma veya içeriği sıkıştırma sürecidir.

lexicalization_scope.note: Çıplak doldurma sonucu ile kap, büyük çanak ve vadiye bağlı gerçekleşmeler ayrı tutulur; yapıya bağlı örnekler genel bir kök anlamına genişletilmez.

concept_map.definition: Bir kabı hareket ettirerek içindekilerin yerleşmesini ve kabın dolmasını ya da sıkışık hale gelmesini sağlamak; uzantı olarak bir şeyi bütünüyle doldurmaktır.

facets.statement: Kabın hareket ettirilmesi, içeriğin yerleşmesini ve kullanılabilir hacmin dolmasını sağlar.
İşlemden doğan tam doluluk veya sıkışık doluluk sonucu ayrıca adlandırılır.
Büyük bir çanağın ya da bir vadinin tamamen dolması sonuç kullanımına örnektir.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Aktarımlar kabı hareket ettirerek içeriği yerleştirme ile doluluk sonucu arasında birleşir; örnekler ölçek kabından çanak ve vadiye uzanır.
